hero.headline: Senate passes $70 billion immigration enforcement bill
hero.body:
The Senate passed a $70 billion immigration enforcement funding bill after an overnight vote. The legislation authorizes substantial funding for border security and immigration operations, advancing through the chamber after Republicans rejected Democratic efforts to permanently ban what has been called Trump's settlement fund.

The bill moved through the Senate during an extended voting session known as a vote-a-rama, where lawmakers considered numerous amendments before final passage. Democrats attempted to include provisions that would place permanent restrictions on a fund they associate with the previous administration, but those efforts failed to gain sufficient support.

The $70 billion authorization represents a significant investment in immigration enforcement infrastructure and operations. The funding is intended to support border patrol activities, detention facilities, immigration courts, and related enforcement programs. The bill now heads to the House of Representatives for consideration.

The legislation comes as immigration policy remains a priority issue in Congress. Republicans have pushed for increased enforcement funding, while Democrats have sought to include oversight measures and restrictions on how the money can be used. The overnight voting process reflected the tensions surrounding immigration legislation, with both parties attempting to shape the final bill through amendments.

Former first lady Jill Biden discussed her husband's 2024 campaign in a separate interview, reflecting on the political landscape that has shaped current policy debates. The passage of the immigration bill marks a significant legislative development, though its ultimate fate depends on action in the House and potential reconciliation with other immigration proposals under consideration.

cards.headline: US economy added 172,000 jobs in May, beating expectations
cards.body:
The US labor market added 172,000 jobs in May, significantly outpacing economist predictions of around 80,000 new positions. The unemployment rate remained steady at 4.3%, according to data from the Bureau of Labor Statistics.

The stronger-than-expected job growth demonstrates continued resilience in the labor market despite rising inflation and economic uncertainty linked to ongoing Middle East conflicts. The May figures also prompted revisions to earlier months, with March and April combined seeing an additional 93,000 jobs added compared to initial reports.

The leisure and hospitality sector drove much of the employment gains as the country prepares to host the World Cup. The Bureau of Labor Statistics identified these industries as significant contributors to May's job creation. Consumer spending on travel and entertainment continues to remain elevated, supporting ongoing hiring in these sectors.

The jobs report provides important data for Federal Reserve policymakers as they assess the economy's direction. With the labor market demonstrating strength rather than weakness, officials have less immediate pressure to cut interest rates. Instead, the Fed has shifted its focus toward addressing resurgent inflation, which continues to squeeze consumers and complicate monetary policy decisions.

The solid employment numbers come after a challenging period for the labor market. Job growth had weakened considerably in recent months, though May's figures suggest a potential recovery is underway. However, economists warn that slow workforce growth may constrain how rapidly the overall economy can expand going forward.

The strong jobs report arrives amid broader economic concerns. Inflation remains unstable, with prices continuing to affect consumer sentiment. The Federal Reserve has indicated that it is proceeding cautiously on interest rate decisions, balancing the need to support employment with efforts to control price increases.

Young people entering the job market continue to face particular headwinds in securing entry-level positions. Economists have raised concerns that these early career obstacles could have lasting effects on lifetime earning potential for this generation of workers.

The May employment data underscores a labor market that remains fundamentally sound even as underlying economic pressures persist. Policymakers will likely reference these figures in upcoming discussions about the appropriate course for monetary policy. The combination of solid job growth and steady unemployment suggests the labor market has found some stability, though inflation concerns remain a central focus for Federal Reserve officials weighing their next moves on interest rates.

cards.headline: US-Brokered Lebanon Cease-Fire Stalls as Israel and Hezbollah Continue Fighting
cards.body:
Efforts to broker a cease-fire between Israel and Hezbollah in Lebanon have stalled despite a new agreement announced by the United States. Fighting between the two sides has intensified even after President Trump announced on Monday that both Israel and Hezbollah had agreed to stop all military operations.

The situation deteriorated quickly. Within hours of Trump's announcement, Israeli warplanes launched dozens of strikes across southern Lebanon. Lebanon's National News Agency reported 30 Israeli strikes on Tuesday alone. Near the city of Sidon, rescue workers recovered the bodies of six family members, including two children and a woman, following one strike. The Israeli military also issued new evacuation warnings for the southern city of Nabatiyeh.

Israel accused Hezbollah of violating the ceasefire, citing what Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu called "repeated and ongoing violations." Netanyahu had ordered strikes on Beirut's southern suburbs, a densely populated Hezbollah stronghold, claiming the group had broken the terms of an earlier ceasefire officially in place since April 17.

Trump reportedly intervened during this escalation. According to news reports, Trump called Netanyahu over the strikes on the Beirut suburbs, and the two reached an agreement that Netanyahu would refrain from attacking that area if Hezbollah ceased its attacks on Israel. However, the situation remained volatile as both sides continued military operations.

Hezbollah has rejected the ceasefire framework. The group maintains it will not accept what it views as a one-sided arrangement requiring it to stop fighting first while Israel continues operations. Mahmoud Qmati, a senior Hezbollah official, told news agencies that the group "will not accept a partial ceasefire" and warned that any aggression against Beirut's southern suburbs "could lead to a deeper and stronger response."

Adding to the complexity, Hezbollah has not been a direct party to the negotiations, complicating Washington's mediation efforts. The group is not formally represented at the talks, leaving unclear who can commit the organization to any agreement.

The latest round of violence represents a significant escalation in the conflict, which began in March following Hezbollah's retaliation for the killing of Iran's supreme leader. Israeli troops have pushed deep into southern Lebanon, raising their flag over Beaufort Castle in what marks their deepest incursion since their occupation ended in 2000.

The breakdown in negotiations has raised concerns about regional stability. Iran's political leadership suspended further negotiations with the United States, declaring that a ceasefire in Lebanon was a precondition for broader talks. Israeli and Lebanese delegations have begun a fourth round of talks in Washington, but without agreement on fundamental terms, prospects for lasting peace remain uncertain.

cards.headline: Nearly 50 Die After Lorry Breaks Down in Sahara Desert
cards.teaser: Only two people survived the ordeal, trekking more than 50 kilometers across the desert to reach authorities.
cards.body:
Nearly 50 people died of thirst in the Sahara desert after their lorry broke down. Only two survivors managed to trek more than 50 kilometers across the desert to reach authorities and alert them to the tragedy.

The incident underscores the extreme dangers faced by people attempting to cross the Sahara under harsh conditions with minimal resources. By the time help arrived, the other passengers had succumbed to dehydration in the desert heat.

cards.headline: Federal Reserve shifts focus to inflation over rate cuts
cards.teaser: Fed officials are prioritizing inflation concerns as the jobs market stabilizes.
cards.body:
Federal Reserve officials have turned their attention to resurgent inflation after a period of focusing on employment concerns. The shift reflects growing confidence in labor market stability, reducing the urgency for interest rate cuts that might stimulate hiring.

The change in priorities comes as policymakers weigh how to balance their dual mandate of maximum employment and stable prices. With jobs data showing continued strength, the Fed now has more room to address inflation without worrying about undermining employment growth.

cards.headline: Senate passes $69.5 billion immigration enforcement bill after overnight session
cards.body:
The Senate voted early Friday to pass a $69.5 billion budget reconciliation package that funds immigration enforcement operations through 2029, following an all-night legislative session. The bill advances a key component of President Trump's immigration agenda, providing multiyear funding for border and interior enforcement activities.

The overnight session included votes on multiple amendments, with some Republican defections complicating passage. GOP senators broke ranks on various measures, including attempts to prohibit funding for President Trump's anti-weaponization fund and a protest vote against William Pulte's appointment to lead a federal agency. The final vote came just before dawn after hours of debate and procedural maneuvering.

The reconciliation process allowed Republicans to pass the legislation with a simple majority rather than the 60 votes typically required to overcome a filibuster. This legislative mechanism has been used by both parties in recent years to advance major spending and tax bills when they control both chambers of Congress and the White House. The $69.5 billion price tag represents a significant investment in immigration enforcement infrastructure and personnel.

The legislation now heads to the House of Representatives, where Republican leadership will need to navigate their own narrow majority to send the bill to President Trump's desk. House passage is expected but not guaranteed, as conservative and moderate factions within the GOP caucus have differed on immigration policy details throughout the current session. The bill's multiyear funding structure aims to provide stability for enforcement operations beyond the typical annual appropriations cycle.

The vote caps months of negotiations over immigration policy and spending levels. Republican leaders had prioritized the legislation as part of their broader agenda on border security, while Democrats largely opposed the measure. The overnight session reflected the tight timeline facing Senate leadership as they work to clear legislative priorities before an upcoming recess.

cards.headline: Italy Calls for New European Military Alliance to Ensure Continental Defense
cards.teaser: Italy's defense minister said European nations should create a joint defense system and take greater responsibility for their own security.
cards.body:
Guido Crosetto, Italy's defense minister, said in an interview that European countries should establish a new military alliance to defend the continent. The proposal calls for European nations to forge a joint defense system rather than relying on existing security arrangements.

Crosetto argued that European countries need to assume greater responsibility for their own security. The proposal comes amid ongoing debates about the future of European defense policy and the continent's relationship with traditional security partners. The Italian defense minister's comments reflect growing discussion among European leaders about the need for stronger independent military capabilities.

cards.headline: US Journalist Pleads Guilty to Working as Agent for China
cards.teaser: Thomas Weir Pauken II, 50, knowingly worked with people employed by the Chinese government for years.
cards.body:
Thomas Weir Pauken II, a 50-year-old US journalist, has pleaded guilty to acting as an agent for the Chinese government. He admitted to knowingly working with individuals employed by China's government over several years.

The case highlights concerns about foreign influence operations within the United States and the recruitment of Americans to serve foreign government interests.

cards.headline: Armenia's Prime Minister Seeks Reelection Amid Questions Over War and Peace
cards.teaser: Nikol Pashinyan faces an election as Armenia weighs questions of war and peace, autocracy and democracy, and independence.
cards.body:
Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan of Armenia is seeking reelection as his country confronts fundamental questions about its future direction. The election comes as Armenia weighs choices between war and peace, autocracy and democracy, and subjugation and independence.

Pashinyan has received backing from the United States while facing opposition from Russia. The prime minister is fighting for his political survival in an election that will help determine Armenia's geopolitical orientation and domestic governance. The contest reflects broader regional tensions as Armenia navigates its relationships with major powers.

cards.headline: Balkan Leaders Attend EU Summit as Membership Expansion Gains Urgency
cards.teaser: European Union leaders are meeting with counterparts from the Western Balkans in Montenegro to discuss accelerated membership prospects.
cards.body:
More than 30 European leaders gathered in the Montenegrin coastal resort of Tivat on Friday to reaffirm membership prospects for six Western Balkan countries. Emmanuel Macron, Friedrich Merz, Giorgia Meloni and Ursula von der Leyen were among those attending the summit aimed at demonstrating that EU membership remains a realistic goal for the region.

The focus of the talks centered on deepening integration of the six Balkan nations—including Montenegro and Albania—into the EU single market as a pathway toward eventual bloc membership. The summit reflects the EU's commitment to expanding eastward, despite existing divisions among member states over how to approach enlargement of the 27-member bloc.

cards.headline: Fury in France After Suspected Child Murderer's Criminal History Revealed
cards.teaser: A man suspected of murdering an 11-year-old girl had previously been identified as a potential child molester, records show.
cards.body:
Public anger has erupted in France following the release of a criminal record for a man suspected of murdering an 11-year-old girl. According to authorities, the suspect had previously been identified as a potential child molester.

The revelation has intensified criticism of how authorities handled the case and monitored individuals flagged as threats to children. The disclosure has sparked broader debate in France about law enforcement's systems for tracking and preventing crimes against children.

cards.headline: Detainees at Alligator Alcatraz facility report coercive conditions
cards.teaser: Immigration detainees say guards withhold food and clean water until they sign documents written in English.
cards.body:
Detainees at Florida's "Alligator Alcatraz" immigration detention facility reported that guards withheld food and fresh water until they signed English-language documents they did not understand. In an audio recording of a call to an immigration advocacy group, more than half a dozen detainees alleged the water provided over three days was contaminated with mosquito larvae, suggesting a coercive tactic.

The reports indicate detainees faced pressure to sign paperwork presented exclusively in English despite language barriers. The allegations raise concerns about conditions and practices at the facility.

cards.headline: Public health departments prepare for World Cup health risks
cards.teaser: Officials plan responses to common ailments and monitor the Ebola outbreak as fans gather for the tournament.
cards.body:
Public health departments are preparing for potential health challenges as fans gather for the World Cup. Local health authorities are developing plans to address common ailments, including insect-borne illnesses, germs, and heat-related conditions that could affect attendees.

Officials are also monitoring the Ebola outbreak amid concerns about disease transmission in crowded settings during the international event. The preparations reflect the health risks associated with large gatherings, though federal involvement has been reduced compared to previous years.

cards.headline: Senate candidate Graham Platner faces new allegations of disturbing behavior toward women
cards.teaser: Multiple reports detail accusations of toxic relationships and unsettling conduct, prompting anger among Democrats.
cards.body:
Graham Platner faces accusations of toxic relationships and disturbing behavior toward women, according to multiple news reports. The allegations come days after a sexting scandal involving the Senate candidate emerged. Platner has denied hurting an ex-girlfriend and stated he will not quit the Senate race.

Democrats have expressed anger over the latest revelations about Platner's conduct. The reports include details of allegedly unsettling behavior toward women over a period of time. The controversy continues to develop as California awaits election results in other races.

cards.headline: Judge spares teen rapists from jail, cites intellectual limitations
cards.teaser: Two boys convicted of rape received youth rehabilitation orders instead of incarceration, causing public outcry.
cards.body:
A judge sentenced two teenage boys convicted of rape to youth rehabilitation orders rather than jail time, citing their intellectual limitations. The sentencing sparked public outcry over concerns that the punishment was inadequate for the severity of the crimes.

Youth rehabilitation orders involve supervision and specific requirements but do not include incarceration. The case has raised questions about how the justice system should balance sentencing considerations for juvenile offenders convicted of serious crimes.

cards.headline: Former student appears in court over University of Surrey crossbow attack
cards.teaser: A university safety officer suffered serious injuries in the attack at the Guildford campus.
cards.body:
A former student appeared in court following a crossbow attack at the University of Surrey campus in Guildford. The incident occurred on Thursday and left a university campus safety officer with serious injuries.

The accused formerly attended the university where the attack took place. The safety officer targeted in the attack remains in serious condition following the assault on the campus grounds.

cards.headline: British military chief warns of most dangerous security period
cards.teaser: Chief of the Defence Staff says Russian incursions into UK defenses risk crossing a line.
cards.body:
Sir Richard Knighton, Britain's Chief of the Defence Staff, has warned that the UK faces its most dangerous security period in his experience. Speaking to the BBC, he highlighted Russian incursions into UK defences as a particular concern, stating they risk crossing a line that could escalate tensions between the nations.

The warning reflects mounting anxieties about military threats to British security and comes as the government reassesses its defence strategy in response to foreign military activities near UK territory and strategic installations.

cards.headline: Young graduates struggle to launch careers in recovering job market
cards.teaser: Recent college graduates face difficulties finding work despite broader labor market improvements.
cards.body:
Recent college graduates are encountering persistent challenges in starting their careers even as the overall labor market has strengthened. The difficulty in securing entry-level positions has raised concerns among economists about long-term consequences for this cohort of workers.

Historical evidence shows that graduating into a weak job market can leave permanent scars on wages and career opportunities. Workers who struggle to find appropriate positions early in their careers often face lower earnings and fewer advancement opportunities for years afterward.

cards.headline: Stock futures decline as chip sector sell-off continues
cards.teaser: S&P 500 and Nasdaq futures dropped as semiconductor stocks extended losses.
cards.body:
Stock market futures fell as semiconductor stocks continued their decline and Treasury yields rose following the release of the jobs report. Both S&P 500 and Nasdaq futures moved lower, threatening the S&P 500's winning streak.

The weakness in chip stocks has weighed on technology-focused indexes as investors reassess valuations in the artificial intelligence sector. The combination of higher yields and sector-specific pressure has created challenges for broader market indices.

cards.headline: Bitcoin falls toward $60,000 as crypto markets tumble
cards.teaser: Bitcoin could drop to $60,000 as cryptocurrencies extend their decline.
cards.body:
Bitcoin continued its slide this week, trading near its 2026 low and now sitting roughly 50 percent below its all-time high. Analysts warned the leading cryptocurrency could fall to $60,000 as selling pressure persists across digital asset markets.

Privacy coins and ether led the latest losses as the broader cryptocurrency market plummeted. Bitcoin recorded its longest losing streak since August, capping a particularly difficult week for digital assets. Zcash dropped 37 percent as privacy-focused tokens faced especially heavy selling.

cards.headline: Anthropic calls for AI nonproliferation measures
cards.teaser: The artificial intelligence company proposed a brake pedal for self-improving AI models.
cards.body:
Anthropic, a major artificial intelligence company, called for nonproliferation measures to protect humanity from self-improving AI models. The company said safeguards are needed as artificial intelligence systems become more advanced and autonomous.

The proposal could have significant consequences for the AI industry, potentially leading to new regulatory frameworks or international agreements. Anthropic's position marks a notable stance from within the technology sector on managing the risks associated with rapidly advancing AI capabilities.

cards.headline: SpaceX shares to become available to individual investors
cards.teaser: Elon Musk's space and AI company will allow retail investors to buy shares starting next week.
cards.body:
Individual investors will be able to purchase shares in SpaceX starting next week, opening access to Elon Musk's rockets and artificial intelligence company beyond institutional buyers. The move represents a shift in how the private space company manages its ownership structure.

SpaceX has remained privately held while building a dominant position in commercial spaceflight and satellite internet services. Allowing individual investors to take stakes could provide the company with additional capital while giving retail investors exposure to the space industry.

hero.headline: Valve confirms Steam Machine console will launch this summer
hero.body:
Valve announced it will release the Steam Machine, its new gaming console, this summer. The company made the confirmation after years of delays and speculation about when the device would reach consumers.

The Steam Machine represents Valve's latest effort to expand beyond its digital storefront into hardware. The console runs on a version of SteamOS and aims to bring PC gaming into the living room. Valve also announced the Steam Frame alongside the main console, though specific technical specifications for either device were not detailed in the announcement.

The company outlined new certification requirements for games on the platform. Titles seeking Steam Machine Verified status must meet specific performance standards. For virtual reality games running in standalone mode, Valve set a minimum frame rate of 72 frames per second, establishing a baseline for VR performance on the system.

The announcement comes as the gaming hardware market continues to evolve, with traditional console makers and PC manufacturers competing for players. Valve previously attempted to enter the console space with an earlier Steam Machine initiative that launched in 2015, which saw multiple hardware partners create systems running SteamOS. That effort largely faded as partners discontinued their models.

This new version appears to be a direct Valve-manufactured product rather than a partnership with multiple hardware makers. The summer launch window suggests the company aims to have units available for the peak gaming season, though Valve has not specified an exact release date or pricing information for either the Steam Machine or Steam Frame.

cards.headline: Microsoft AI chief criticizes Anthropic models as too expensive
cards.teaser: Microsoft's AI division leader said Anthropic's artificial intelligence models cost too much for practical deployment.
cards.body:
Microsoft's artificial intelligence chief stated that Anthropic's AI models carry prices that make them difficult to justify for widespread use. The comments come as Microsoft continues developing its own AI capabilities and partnerships in the rapidly growing sector.

The statement reflects ongoing competition and tension in the AI industry over model pricing and performance. Microsoft has invested heavily in OpenAI and integrated AI features across its product lineup, including Windows and Azure cloud services. The company recently announced Project Solara, an Android-based operating system designed specifically for AI agents rather than traditional applications.

cards.headline: Anthropic revenue reaches $47 billion annually ahead of planned IPO
cards.teaser: The AI company reported annualized revenue crossed $47 billion in May, up sharply from roughly $9 billion at the end of 2025.
cards.body:
Anthropic's annualized revenue reached $47 billion in May, a dramatic jump from approximately $9 billion at the end of 2025. The company is preparing for an IPO amid this rapid expansion.

President Daniela Amodei addressed concerns about whether AI companies can deliver returns matching their valuations and sustain their growth trajectories. Her comments reflect confidence in the company's trajectory despite broader industry questions about the long-term profitability of large language model development.

cards.headline: Former OpenAI executive Mira Murati increases public presence
cards.teaser: Mira Murati, who previously held a leadership role at OpenAI, has begun making more public appearances.
cards.body:
Mira Murati has stepped back into the spotlight following her departure from OpenAI. In today's competitive tech landscape, maintaining visibility has become essential for industry leaders—staying quiet offers diminishing returns when the goal is to keep the market aware of your presence.

Murati's increased public profile reflects the strategic importance of maintaining relevance as the AI sector evolves rapidly. Her movements continue to draw attention from investors and technologists monitoring leadership changes in artificial intelligence.

cards.headline: Geomagnetic storm could bring northern lights to Utah and other states
cards.teaser: A powerful geomagnetic storm may make the aurora borealis visible across several U.S. states including Utah, North Carolina, Vermont, and areas as far south as Illinois.
cards.body:
Forecasters issued a G3 geomagnetic storm watch for the period covering June 4-5. Four Earth-directed coronal mass ejections are moving toward the planet, which could trigger auroral displays at lower latitudes than typically see them.

The Space Weather Prediction Center updated its aurora forecast to include states well south of the usual northern tier viewing areas. Residents in Illinois and Oregon may have opportunities to see the phenomenon, with viewing conditions depending on local weather and light pollution levels.

cards.headline: Paleontologists identify new four-winged dinosaur species in China
cards.teaser: Researchers discovered a new species related to Velociraptor that had four wings and likely hunted birds from trees in ancient China.
cards.body:
Scientists have discovered a previously unknown microraptorine dinosaur in China that possessed wing-like structures on all four limbs. The creature is a relative of the Velociraptor and represents a distinct approach to aerial hunting among dinosaurs.

The fossil evidence indicates this four-winged dinosaur used gliding flight to hunt from trees in its ancient forest habitat, similar to how modern flying squirrels move through the air. The discovery, co-led by the Carnegie Museum paleontology team, provides new insights into how different dinosaur lineages developed flight capabilities and occupied specialized ecological roles as aerial predators.

cards.headline: Airbnb CEO plans to establish dedicated AI research lab
cards.teaser: Brian Chesky announced plans to launch an artificial intelligence lab at Airbnb to develop the company's own capabilities.
cards.body:
Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky announced plans to launch a new AI lab as the company builds internal artificial intelligence capabilities. Chesky previously explained that Airbnb had not partnered with existing large language model providers because available products did not meet the company's needs.

The move reflects Airbnb's strategy to develop proprietary AI technology tailored to its platform rather than relying on third-party solutions.

hero.headline: Polish qualifier Chwalinska reaches French Open final
hero.body:
Maja Chwalinska, a Polish qualifier, has reached the French Open final in one of the most improbable runs in Grand Slam history. The 24-year-old defeated Diana Shnaider 7-6 (4), 6-4 in the semifinals to secure her place in Saturday's championship match.

Chwalinska's achievement is historic. She is the first qualifier ever to reach the French Open final and only the second qualifier to reach any Grand Slam final, following Emma Raducanu's run at the 2021 US Open. During her three-week journey through the qualifying draw and main draw, she has won nine matches while losing just one set.

The emotional toll of her success was evident after her victory. "Like a dream, honestly. I don't know what's going on," Chwalinska said. "I don't know what to say." She later reflected on the improbability of her run, saying "Let's not pretend someone expected it. I mean, I was outside top 100 and now I'm in the finals of a grand slam, so I feel like it's a big thing. So it's hard to process it."

Before this tournament, Chwalinska had competed professionally for a decade without reaching the top 100. Her current ranking of 114 sits just one spot behind her career high. She had won only one main draw match at a Grand Slam prior to Roland Garros, coming at Wimbledon in 2022.

Her opponent in the final will be Mirra Andreeva, the eighth seed, who defeated Marta Kostyuk 6-1, 6-3 in her semifinal. The matchup sets up a final between two players who were not considered title favorites at the tournament's start.

The financial reward for Chwalinska's run has been substantial. Her prize money of $1,626,744 nearly doubles the $864,030 she had earned throughout her entire career. The substantial paycheck comes after she faced uncertainty during her tournament run about being able to afford her hotel expenses until Polish drinks company Oshee stepped in to help.

Despite her physical disadvantages on the court, Chwalinska has succeeded through tactical skill and intelligence. At 1.64 meters tall, she is diminutive for professional tennis and lacks the power of many competitors. She has compensated by using slices, angles, and drop shots to confound opponents and disrupt their rhythm.

Her semifinal opponent, Shnaider, had pulled off a stunning upset herself by defeating world number one Aryna Sabalenka in the quarterfinals after recovering from 6-3, 4-1 down. However, Shnaider could not back up that monumental win against Chwalinska's crafty and intelligent play.

The French Open final will determine which player claims their first Grand Slam title.

cards.headline: Leclerc leads Hamilton in Monaco Grand Prix first practice
cards.teaser: Charles Leclerc topped Lewis Hamilton in a Ferrari one-two during first practice at the Monaco Grand Prix.
cards.body:
Charles Leclerc set the pace in the opening practice session at the Monaco Grand Prix, with Ferrari teammate Lewis Hamilton finishing second. The two drivers secured a dominant one-two finish as teams began their weekend preparations on the challenging street circuit.

Red Bull faced early difficulties when Isack Hadjar crashed his car during the session, dealing a setback to the team's Monaco weekend.

cards.headline: Robinson takes five wickets on Test return for England
cards.teaser: Ollie Robinson completed a five-wicket haul in his return to Test cricket for England against New Zealand at Lord's.
cards.body:
England bowler Ollie Robinson marked his return to Test cricket with a five-wicket haul against New Zealand at Lord's. The performance highlighted his successful comeback to international cricket after a period away from the team.

Robinson's impressive bowling display put England in a strong position in the match. By the end of day one, New Zealand had reached 61-6, trailing England by 79 runs, as Robinson's performance helped restrict the visitors' batting lineup.

cards.headline: Tottenham sign Robertson after Liverpool departure
cards.teaser: Tottenham completed the signing of Scotland captain Andy Robertson following his exit from Liverpool at the end of his contract.
cards.body:
Andy Robertson joined Tottenham after leaving Liverpool as a free agent. The Scotland captain's contract with Liverpool expired, allowing him to move to the north London club without a transfer fee.

Robertson had been a regular at Liverpool before his departure. The left back brings international experience to Tottenham, where he will compete for a starting position in the squad.

cards.headline: Lions coach Campbell mocks Myles Garrett trade reactions
cards.teaser: Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell responded to criticism surrounding the team's trade involving Cleveland Browns defensive end Myles Garrett.
cards.body:
Dan Campbell addressed public reaction to the Myles Garrett trade in remarks that appeared to dismiss concerns about the deal. The Lions coach's comments came after the team completed a transaction with the Cleveland Browns involving the star defensive end.

The trade included draft pick compensation and was the result of a two-month negotiation between the Rams and Browns organizations. Some NFL fans and analysts have debated which team benefited most from the agreement.

cards.headline: Feyi-Waboso faces surgery for facial injury
cards.teaser: England winger Immanuel Feyi-Waboso will undergo surgery for a facial injury that could sideline him for the remainder of the season.
cards.body:
England winger Immanuel Feyi-Waboso will undergo surgery for a facial injury sustained during competition. The procedure could sideline him for the remainder of the Premier League season.

The injury marks a significant blow to Feyi-Waboso's campaign and England's attacking options heading into the latter stages of the season.

cards.headline: Shaw and Hasegawa shortlisted for PFA women's award
cards.teaser: Manchester City forwards Khadija Shaw and Yui Hasegawa earned nominations for the PFA Women's Player of the Year award.
cards.body:
Manchester City duo Khadija Shaw and Yui Hasegawa have been shortlisted for the Professional Footballers Association's Women's Player of the Year award. Both players are in contention for the prestigious individual honor.

The PFA award is voted on by fellow professional players, making it one of the most respected accolades in women's football.

hero.headline: Actor James Handy killed in stabbing at California home
hero.body:
Veteran actor James Handy, 81, was fatally stabbed at his home in Tarzana, California on Wednesday morning. He was discovered in the front yard with multiple stab wounds to the chest and was unconscious when found at 9:30am. He was pronounced dead at the scene.

Michael Gledhill, 44, the son of Handy's girlfriend, has been arrested and charged with murder. Bail was set at $2 million. According to Los Angeles police, Gledhill resided at the location with his mother, who is Handy's girlfriend.

A 911 caller reported the incident with the statement: "I am the son of man, I just killed the man of sin." When officers arrived at the scene, Gledhill told them he was "the one they were looking for," according to the police statement.

Handy had built a lengthy career in film and television spanning nearly five decades. He was born in New York City and began his acting career in 1977 on the television series Ryan's Hope. Over the years, he appeared in numerous productions across different genres and formats.

His film credits include character roles in Jumanji, Top Gun: Maverick, and Logan. He also appeared in K-911 and had television roles in shows including Law and Order, NCIS: Los Angeles, and Criminal Minds. His most recent film appearance was in Top Gun: Maverick in 2022.

Handy was known for taking supporting roles that allowed him to showcase his range as a character actor. These parts spanned major studio productions as well as smaller projects throughout his career.

The Los Angeles Police Department responded to the scene and conducted an investigation into the circumstances of the stabbing. The killing marks another violent incident in the Los Angeles area involving a member of the entertainment community.

Handy's death concludes a career marked by consistent work in Hollywood over many decades. His steady presence in the industry was built through character work across film and television, contributing to productions that reached audiences both large and small.

cards.headline: Mobo Awards founder Kanya King dies at 57
cards.teaser: The music industry executive and cultural figure died from cancer.
cards.body:
Kanya King, founder of the Mobo Awards, died from cancer at age 57. The music executive created the awards show that recognized achievements in music of black origin and became a major platform for artists in the UK and internationally.

Sir Idris Elba, Alesha Dixon, and Stormzy were among those paying tribute to King following news of her death. The Mobo Awards, which she established, became an important institution in British music culture, celebrating artists across multiple genres including hip-hop, grime, R&B, and gospel over its decades-long run.

cards.headline: Ed Sheeran performs surprise waterfront show for fans
cards.teaser: The singer played half a dozen songs during an early-morning performance.
cards.body:
Ed Sheeran performed an impromptu concert at a waterfront location, drawing hundreds of fans to the unexpected show. The singer played approximately six songs during the early-morning performance, giving attendees an intimate concert experience outside of his scheduled tour dates.

The surprise appearance gave fans a rare chance to see the British artist in a casual, unplanned setting. Sheeran has occasionally staged similar impromptu performances throughout his career, often in smaller venues or public spaces, as a way to connect with audiences outside traditional concert halls.

cards.headline: Brad Pitt on set as motorcycle racing film begins production on Isle of Man
cards.teaser: The Amazon MGM Studios project stars Channing Tatum and Eve Hewson.
cards.body:
Brad Pitt is on location for the motorcycle racing film Isle of Man, which began shooting on the island nation in the Irish Sea. The Amazon MGM Studios production, produced by Pitt's Plan B company, stars Channing Tatum and Eve Hewson. Filming started approximately one week ago, coinciding with the iconic motorcycle race held on the island.

The production is taking advantage of the Isle of Man's status as home to one of the most famous motorcycle racing events in the world. The timing of the shoot allows filmmakers to capture the atmosphere and setting of the actual race, which draws competitors and spectators from around the globe each year.

cards.headline: Steve Lacy releases single ahead of third album
cards.teaser: The musician will release Oh Yeah? in July.
cards.body:
Steve Lacy released a new single titled The Feeling, previewing his upcoming third studio album. The track marks the first material from Oh Yeah?, which the musician plans to release in July. The song explores themes of longing and romantic uncertainty.

Lacy has built his career as both a solo artist and as a member of the band The Internet. His previous albums established him as a distinctive voice in contemporary R&B and alternative music, earning critical recognition and a devoted following. The new album will be his first full-length release since his previous record.

cards.headline: Primavera festival attendees criticize weather response on opening day
cards.teaser: Fans said organizers lacked a backup plan for bad weather in Barcelona.
cards.body:
Primavera festival attendees in Barcelona expressed frustration with organizers' response to bad weather on the opening day. Fans were confused about the lack of a backup plan when adverse conditions affected the outdoor event.

The incident dampened attendees' experience of the first day's performances, with complaints surfacing on social media about how the situation was handled.

cards.headline: Chinese film Dear You expands to international theaters
cards.teaser: The Teochew-dialect family drama has been a box office success in China.
cards.body:
Dear You, a Teochew-dialect drama that became one of China's major box office performers in 2026, will expand to international markets starting June 18. Damai Entertainment, formerly known as Alibaba Pictures, is handling the worldwide theatrical release. The film follows Xiaowei, a young grandson navigating family relationships.

Directed by Lan Hongchun, the family drama has resonated with Chinese audiences and emerged as a defining commercial success story this year. The international expansion represents an effort to bring Chinese-language cinema to broader audiences outside the domestic market, where the film has already established its financial credentials.

hero.headline: Senate passes $69.5 billion immigration enforcement bill after overnight session
hero.body:
The Senate voted early Friday to pass a $69.5 billion budget reconciliation package that funds immigration enforcement operations through 2029, following an all-night legislative session. The bill advances a key component of President Trump's immigration agenda, providing multiyear funding for border and interior enforcement activities.

The overnight session included votes on multiple amendments, with some Republican defections complicating passage. GOP senators broke ranks on various measures, including attempts to prohibit funding for President Trump's anti-weaponization fund and a protest vote against William Pulte's appointment to lead a federal agency. The final vote came just before dawn after hours of debate and procedural maneuvering.

The reconciliation process allowed Republicans to pass the legislation with a simple majority rather than the 60 votes typically required to overcome a filibuster. This legislative mechanism has been used by both parties in recent years to advance major spending and tax bills when they control both chambers of Congress and the White House. The $69.5 billion price tag represents a significant investment in immigration enforcement infrastructure and personnel.

The legislation now heads to the House of Representatives, where Republican leadership will need to navigate their own narrow majority to send the bill to President Trump's desk. House passage is expected but not guaranteed, as conservative and moderate factions within the GOP caucus have differed on immigration policy details throughout the current session. The bill's multiyear funding structure aims to provide stability for enforcement operations beyond the typical annual appropriations cycle.

The vote caps months of negotiations over immigration policy and spending levels. Republican leaders had prioritized the legislation as part of their broader agenda on border security, while Democrats largely opposed the measure. The overnight session reflected the tight timeline facing Senate leadership as they work to clear legislative priorities before an upcoming recess.

cards.headline: Six Republicans join Democrats to block FISA extension vote
cards.teaser: Republican senators Josh Hawley, Mike Lee, Rand Paul, Eric Schmitt, Rick Scott, and one other joined Democrats to defeat a procedural motion on extending warrantless surveillance powers.
cards.body:
The Senate voted 47 to 52 early Friday against advancing legislation to extend warrantless spy powers set to expire next week. Six Republican senators broke with their party to join Democrats in blocking the measure.

Sens. Josh Hawley of Missouri, Mike Lee of Utah, Rand Paul of Kentucky, Eric Schmitt of Missouri, and Rick Scott joined Democrats in opposing the procedural vote. The defeat complicates Republican efforts to renew the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act authorities before they lapse.

cards.headline: Deb Haaland wins New Mexico Democratic primary for governor
cards.teaser: Former Interior Secretary Deb Haaland secured the Democratic nomination for New Mexico governor and could become the first female Native American governor if elected in November.
cards.body:
Deb Haaland, who served as Interior Secretary in the Biden administration, won the Democratic primary for New Mexico governor. The victory positions her for a general election campaign that could result in a historic first.

If elected in November, Haaland would become the first female Native American governor in United States history. She previously made history as one of the first two Native American women elected to Congress before joining President Biden's cabinet.

cards.headline: Trump attacks Fox News contributor Karl Rove on social media
cards.teaser: President Trump called for Fox News to remove Karl Rove from the network, referring to the former Republican White House aide as a "sloppy RINO."
cards.body:
President Trump posted on Truth Social calling for Fox News to remove contributor Karl Rove from the network. Trump referred to Rove, a former aide in the George W. Bush White House, as a "sloppy RINO," using the acronym for "Republicans in name only."

Trump wrote that Rove "has called ME and MAGA wrong" in his criticism of the former Bush administration official. Rove has served as a political analyst for Fox News and has previously offered commentary critical of Trump's political strategy and electoral predictions.

cards.headline: Steve Hilton and Xavier Becerra lead California gubernatorial primary
cards.teaser: Early results show Republican Steve Hilton and Democrat Xavier Becerra ahead in California's open primary to replace Gov. Gavin Newsom.
cards.body:
Republican Steve Hilton, a former Fox News host, and Democrat Xavier Becerra are leading in early returns from California's gubernatorial primary. The race features multiple candidates from both parties competing to succeed Gov. Gavin Newsom.

Other Democrats in the race include Katie Porter and Tom Steyer, while Republican Chad Bianco is also running. California uses a top-two primary system where the leading candidates from any party advance to the general election regardless of party affiliation.

cards.headline: Trump plans to attend NBA Finals game at Madison Square Garden
cards.teaser: President Trump said he will attend an NBA Finals game next week at Madison Square Garden after receiving an invitation from Knicks owner James Dolan.
cards.body:
President Trump confirmed he will attend an NBA Finals game at Madison Square Garden next week, telling reporters in the Oval Office that Knicks owner James Dolan extended an invitation. Trump, a longtime Knicks fan and New York native, said "the answer is yes" when asked about the invitation.

Trump has maintained ties to New York sports franchises throughout his political career. The appearance would mark a high-profile public outing for the president at one of the country's most recognizable sports venues during the championship series.

cards.headline: Maine Senate candidate faces new allegations about past relationships
cards.teaser: Graham Platner, running for Senate in Maine, is responding to a New York Times report detailing allegations from women about his behavior in past relationships.
cards.body:
Graham Platner, the Democratic candidate for Senate in Maine, faces scrutiny following a New York Times report containing allegations from women about his past behavior in relationships. Platner has responded to the claims, pushing back on what he characterized as the most serious allegations.

Platner dismissed suggestions that he would withdraw from the Senate race. The candidate is continuing his campaign despite the controversy surrounding the report and its allegations about his personal conduct.
